author: Reuters
description:
GPT-6.1 Astra showed deceptive behavior and tried to use external tools despite knowing it would be unsafe

OpenAI is scrapping the release of GPT-6.1 Astra, a next-generation ⁠AI model planned for an October debut, over safety concerns raised by researchers ⁠during internal testing, the ⁠Wall ​Street Journal reported on Monday.

The model, expected to appear in ChatGPT and ⁠Codex, was designed to handle more complex tasks without human assistance, the report said.

Continue reading...
title: OpenAI scraps release of new model over safety concerns in internal testing

author: Associated Press
description:
Lawyers for Christa Pike, 50, convicted of killing classmate in Knoxville in 1995, ask supreme court to grant stay

Christa Pike was 18 when she killed a classmate in a jealous rage and became one of the youngest women to be sent to death row. Now 50, she is scheduled to be put to death on Wednesday in what would be Tennessee’s first execution of a woman in 200 years.

Pike and her boyfriend were convicted in the 1995 killing of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer, their classmate at Knoxville Job Corps. Prosecutors said Pike feared Slemmer was a romantic rival and lured her to a secluded area where she and her boyfriend tortured and killed Slemmer.

Continue reading...
title: Tennessee to execute a woman for first time in 200 years after governor denies clemency

author: Associated Press
description:
Decision from conservative justice comes before court hears case on whether fossil-fuel firms deceived US public

Supreme court justice Samuel Alito recused himself Monday from a major climate-change case after facing calls to step aside due to stock holdings in oil companies.

A letter posted in the case did not specify a reason, but the conservative justice has previously recused himself from other cases involving companies where he holds stock.

Continue reading...
title: Samuel Alito steps aside in a major climate case amid scrutiny over oil stock holdings

author: Martin Farrer
description:
Follow the day’s news live.

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The treasurer, Jim Chalmers, has defended his economic record on the eve of what is widely expected to be the fourth interest rate rise of 2026, as the Reserve Bank remains concerned about persistent inflation.

The RBA board is poised to hike the cash rate from 4.35% to 4.6% on Tuesday, which would be the fourth increase in 2026 and push typical home loan interest rates to 6.5%.

We have a lot going for us and we’ve got a lot of work to do to make sure that in these difficult global circumstances Australia continues to out-perform the world.

We have a big inflation challenge in our economy. It’s made much worse by decisions taken
title: Australia news live: Chalmers defends record as RBA’s cash rate decision due

author: Maya Yang
description:
Danette Colbert and Rickey White sentenced in Adan Manzano’s death for racketeering and negligent homicide

A Louisiana judge has handed lengthy prison sentences to two people convicted of roles in a criminal enterprise that targeted New Orleans tourists led to the death of a reporter covering the 2025 Super Bowl there.

Nancy Miller, a state court judge, on Monday sentenced Danette Colbert, 49, to a total of 60 years in prison: fifty years for racketeering and a consecutive 10 years for negligent homicide in the death of Adan Manzano, a journalist for the Spanish-language news outlet Telemundo Kansas City.

Continue reading...
title: Two people sentenced to 60 and 45 years in prison in death of Telemundo reporter

author: Graham Readfearn Environment and climate correspondent
description:
Carbon Impacts Tracer can be used to estimate climate impact from emissions across eight different factors, including lost food production

The biggest coal project before authorities in New South Wales, the HVO mine, will emit the equivalent of about 809m tonnes of climate-warming carbon dioxide if it wins approval.

That number, for most people, will carry little meaning, as might the calculation that adding that amount of greenhouse gas to the atmosphere will cause an extra 0.00036C of global heating.

But what if the public was instead told that that amount of carbon dioxide would expose almost half a million people to unprecedented heat, or kill nearly 15 million coral colonies on the Great Barrier Reef every time it bleaches?

All those statistics come from a new tool that translates the emissions from bu
title: New tool directly links carbon emissions to amount of environmental and economic damage caused

author: Joseph Gedeon in Washington
description:
President seeks midterms boost as White House says project, built by Indian-owned company, will begin in 2030

Donald Trump on Monday announced what he called the largest steel plant in American history to be built in Iowa, giving Republicans a jobs message to take to voters in a state that could help decide control of the Senate in November.

“Using advanced steelmaking technology, the plant will produce some of the highest quality, most affordable steel anywhere in the world,” Trump said in the Oval Office, flanked by Iowa’s top Republicans.

Continue reading...
title: Trump unveils plan for $15bn Iowa steel plant he calls biggest in US history

author: Associated Press
description:
Police said Tasia Fortune, 29, was killed before her body was placed in the tree, and the scene was ‘staged’

A Mississippi judge set a $5m bond on Monday for a third man charged in the death of a Black woman whose body was found hanging from a tree in August.

Police disclosed on Friday that Tasia Fortune, 29, was killed before her body was placed in a tree behind an abandoned house in Jackson, Mississippi’s capital city.

Guardian staff contributed reporting

Continue reading...
title: Judge sets $5m bond for third suspect in killing of Black woman hung from tree in Mississippi

author: Charlie Moloney
description:
Former journalist and honorary life president of Norwich City FC died peacefully at home on Monday

Michael Wynn-Jones, the journalist and husband of the TV chef Delia Smith, has died at the age of 85.

Wynn-Jones was honorary life president of Norwich City football club, which said everyone at the club was “deeply saddened” by his death.

Continue reading...
title: Michael Wynn-Jones, husband of Delia Smith, dies aged 85

author: Daniel Boffey Chief reporter
description:
Row comes amid rising division and a tendency towards cynical political posturing in Northern Ireland

Three decades ago, it took the deaths of three Roman Catholic children – the Quinn brothers, Jason, nine, Mark, 10, and 11-year-old Richard – in a petrol bomb attack to bring an end to the Drumcree dispute. “No road is worth a life, let alone the lives of three little boys,” the Orange Order’s County Armagh chaplain said at the time.

It is perhaps extraordinary to think that this could ever have needed saying – but that was then. Northern Ireland is very different place today.

Continue reading...
title: Absence of violence in Drumcree does not make standoff any less significant

author: Victoria Bekiempis
description:
CDC says 392 cases of Dengue were reported for the year so far in the state, along with different county-level data

Several Florida counties recently declared a state of local emergency in response to a spate of dengue fever infections.

Hillsborough county, Florida, officials made the declaration on 24 September as health authorities recorded 134 confirmed cases of dengue fever, which is a mosquito-borne sickness typically found in countries outside the US. Officials said that the spread of the illness poses “an immediate and widespread threat to the public health, safety, and welfare of the residents and visitors of Hillsborough county”.

Continue reading...
title: Dengue fever outbreak prompts Florida counties to declare state of emergency

author: Dan Sabbagh Defence and security editor
description:
Tehran has been trying to step up attacks on targets in the west but its track record has been mixed

Investigators may be some way from determining exactly what led five men with three vans to a village just outside RAF Fairford in the small hours of Sunday – but the fact they have all been released on bail without immediate charge suggests they are not deemed to pose a serious and violent threat.

In a moment where wider geopolitical tensions mean external threats are perceived to be close, the question of whether Iran had a hand in the alleged plot remains open. Nonetheless, the bailing of the men is a mercifully lower-key development in an investigation that appeared of the utmost gravity.

Continue reading...
title: Questions remain over Iran’s link to alleged RAF Fairford bomb plot

author: Richard Luscombe
description:
Case of alleged hazing at the University of Arizona is latest in series of controversial incidents involving US fraternities

A college fraternity at the University of Arizona has been suspended after new members were allegedly plied with alcohol and forced to swallow live goldfish.

College officials informed the university’s Sigma Tau Gamma chapter by letter earlier in September that it was under investigation for multiple alleged violations of the student code of conduct, including “endangering, threatening, or causing physical harm” to members of the campus community.

Continue reading...
title: Arizona frat suspended after allegedly making new recruits swallow live goldfish

author: Maya Yang
description:
Billy B Van’s 1919 comedy Van-ar-chy found by student in Sendai will be shown in early November in New Hampshire

A silent comedy filmed in New Hampshire more than a century ago was recently found in Japan, and plans have been set to show the film in early November in the state where it was created.

Van-ar-chy, a 1919 film starring the US entertainer and film-maker Billy B Van, was rediscovered by Kohei Okita, a film student in Sendai, Japan. While researching early cinema related to the word “anarchy”, Okita bought several old film reels at an antique store in Japan and found the comedy starring Van, whom he did not recognize, according to a Van-ar-chy news release.
title: Century-old silent film made in New Hampshire found in Japan antique shop

author: Ben Quinn and Alexandra Topping
description:
Culture secretary criticises Reform leader after he tried to link suspected bomb plot to small boat crossings

Nigel Farage has been described as a “master of the conspiracy theory” by the culture secretary, Lisa Nandy, , after he tried to link events at RAF Fairford to small boat crossings.

The Reform UK leader was criticised over his reaction to the arrests of the men on Sunday, when he said he had been warning for months about “Iranian agents” coming into the UK across the Channel in small boats.

Continue reading...
title: Nandy labels Farage ‘master of conspiracy theory’ over Fairford claims

author: Charlie Moloney
description:
Local fire and rescue service says last week’s tragic incident highlights risks the batteries can pose

A fire that left a mother and her three children dead was caused by a lithium-ion battery, firefighters in Merseyside have said.

An electrical event caused the battery, of a type commonly used in vapes, ebikes and e-scooters, to go into “thermal runaway”, Merseyside fire and rescue service said.

Continue reading...
title: Merseyside blaze that killed mother and three children caused by lithium-ion battery

author: Ariana Baio
description:
Bailey, who oversaw some of Trump’s election crackdown investigations, to resign about a year after assuming role

Andrew Bailey, a deputy director of the FBI who has been overseeing some of Trump’s election-related investigations, will step down from his position approximately one year after assuming his role.

“I am announcing that I am stepping down to return to my family in Missouri,” Bailey wrote in an X post on Monday amid an ongoing shake-up at the bureau.

Continue reading...
title: FBI co-deputy director Andrew Bailey steps down amid agency shake-up

author: Ariana Baio
description:
Bo French, who is running to lead a state agency, has in the past posted controversial and racist statements online

Bo French, a Texas Republican running to lead a powerful state agency, has a history of making controversial social media posts, including calling for the public execution of Democratic leaders, according to a recent investigation from CNN’s KFile team.

French, who is running to lead Texas’s railroad commission, has recently faced criticism from members of his own party after making a racist post on social media. Powerful Republicans, including Texas senator John Cornyn, said they would not support French in the upcoming election.

Continue reading...
title: Texas Republican called for public execution of Democratic leaders – report

author: Jessica Elgot
description:
Conference speech to announce housing associations cannot reject homeless families without good reason as councils gain new powers

Housing associations in England will be told they cannot decline to house homeless families without good reason, Angela Rayner will tell the Labour conference, as part of a drive for more public control of housing.

Homelessness charities said the new powers were a “gamechanger” and had the potential to make a significant difference to rough sleeping and families in temporary accommodation, the numbers of which have risen sharply. Almost 180,000 children are living in temporary accommodation.

Continue reading...
title: Angela Rayner promises greater public control of housing in England

author: Aamna Mohdin Community affairs correspondent
description:
Anger over Israel’s war in Gaza is mobilising British voters, according to Aimee Shalan

Palestine has become a domestic electoral issue in Britain for the first time, according to the incoming head of the country’s largest Palestinian solidarity organisation.

Aimee Shalan, who will take over as director of the Palestine Solidarity Campaign (PSC) in November, joins the organisation as demonstrations against Israel’s war in Gaza have snowballed into what organisers describe as one of the most sustained protest movements in modern British history.

Continue reading...
title: Palestine has become electoral issue in UK for first time, says solidarity campaign chief

author: Carlos Mureithi in Nairobi and agencies
description:
Marie-Celestin Karondwa was attacked on Sunday after promoting measures to prevent spread of disease, his party says

A senior member of the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s ruling party was beaten to death on Sunday after appearing on a radio programme to raise awareness about the Ebola outbreak, a party representative has said.

Marie-Celestin Karondwa, the acting president of the Union for Democracy and Social Progress (UDPS) party’s federal executive committee in Butembo, a new hotspot for the outbreak, was attacked after taking part in a ​radio show during which he ‌promoted prevention measures for the disease, ‌the UDPS federation in the city said in a statement, Reuters reported.

Continue reading...
title: DRC politician beaten to death after radio appearance about Ebola outbreak

author: Nicola Davis Science correspondent
description:
Scientific breakthrough could reduce food waste and make it easier to add the fruit to prepackaged food

It is the bane of every fruit bowl: sliced banana that turns brown before it has reached the table. But such woes could soon be a thing of the past, with gene-edited bananas that keep their freshly peeled colour now one step closer to reaching British shoppers.

According to Tropic, the Norwich-based agricultural-biotechnology company that developed the fruit, the bananas have the same taste and texture but stay “fresh, yellow and appetising long after peeling and slicing”.

Continue reading...
title: Gene-edited bananas that don’t go brown could hit UK supermarkets

author: Pjotr Sauer in Kyiv
description:
Three others wounded as jet-powered drones increasingly target Ukraine’s capital, with medical centre also hit

  • Europe live – latest updates

Russia has hit the National Academy of Sciences in central Kyiv with a drone, killing at least one person in the latest daytime attack on Ukraine’s capital.

Flames tore through the historic building on Monday as people clambered out of first- and second-floor windows to escape, in dramatic scenes increasingly familiar in the heavily bombarded city.

Continue reading...
title: Russian strike on Kyiv’s science academy kills at least one in latest daytime attack

author: Richard Luscombe
description:
Outrage over treatment of alleged offenders, members of Chi Phi fraternity, has grown since lawsuit was made public

  • Sign up for the Breaking News US newsletter email

Prosecutors in New York said on Monday that they have reopened an investigation into the alleged gang-rape of a student at Cornell University after an outcry over “leniency” shown to seven fraternity members named as the perpetrators.

According to lawyers for the student, who filed a civil lawsuit against the university and her alleged attackers e
title: Investigation of alleged gang-rape at Cornell University fraternity house reopened

author: Vikram Dodd Police and crime correspondent
description:
Attack on two Jewish men in north London earlier this year was originally treated as terrorism

The stabbings of two Jewish men in Golders Green, north London, in April are being treated as an alleged hate crime not a terrorist attack, police have said.

Essa Suleiman, 45, was arrested by the Metropolitan police on suspicion of attempted murder shortly after the stabbings on 29 April.

Continue reading...
title: Police treating Golders Green stabbings as suspected hate crime

author: Andrew Messenger
description:
Statistics showed there is ‘almost no chance’ a complaint made against a government department like the police would be investigated independently, expert says

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Queensland’s anti-corruption commission has investigated just 20 of more than 6,000 complaints of suspected corruption in the past year, as the state government comes under renewed pressure to implement a years-late recommendation to end the practice of police investigating police.

The statistic was revealed in Queensland’s Crime and Corruption Commission’s annual report, tabled in s
title: Queensland anti-corruption commission investigated just 20 of more than 6,000 complaints in a year

author: Patrick Commins Economics editor
description:
With RBA predicted to lift cash rate for fourth time this year on Tuesday, experts warn a fifth – or even sixth – rise would be ‘overkill’

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

Two or even three more Reserve Bank interest rate hikes would be “devastating” for the property market but still leave housing more unaffordable than ever as higher borrowing costs trump lower prices, experts say.

The RBA’s monetary policy board is widely expected on Tuesday afternoon to announce an increase in its cash rate to 4.6%, from 4.35%, in a decision that will add another $100 to the monthly mortgage interes
title: Further interest rate hikes could ‘devastate’ property market without easing unaffordability

author: Pippa Neill Environment reporter
description:
People living next to a chemicals plant near Blackpool were tested for ‘forever chemicals’; last week they received the alarming results

Last February, I got a call from a woman called Sam Hammond. We had been speaking on and off for a while over her growing concern that her garden could be affected by pollution from a nearby chemical plant.

That morning, Sam had been hand-delivered a letter from her council informing her that her pet ducks’ eggs, reared in her garden, were contaminated with Pfas chemicals.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Are these chemicals in my blood?’: How one community learned the truth about Pfas pollution

author: Ian Sample Science editor
description:
Mission goes ahead despite some fears an initial engine failure after the Texas launch would scupper the attempt

SpaceX has sent its enormous Starship rocket into Earth’s orbit for the first time on a milestone flight intended to pave the way for future missions to the moon and Mars.

The rocket, the largest and most powerful ever built, blasted off from SpaceX’s Starbase launch facility in Texas at 7.48am local time (1.48pm BST) marking its 14th test flight and first attempt to circle the planet before falling back to Earth.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Starship is in orbit’: cheers go up as huge SpaceX rocket circles Earth for first time

author: Sarah Butler
description:
Supermarket chain declares ‘increasing confidence’ in its growth plans after posting record annual revenue of £19bn

  • Business live – latest updates

Aldi says it is stepping up investment in the UK with plans to spend £900m and open more than 40 stores.

The company, which operates 1,092 budget supermarkets in the UK and Ireland, revealed sales rose 5% to a record £19bn last year. It opened 40 stores but profits slipped by £2.6m to £433m as it cut prices despite cost inflation.

Continue reading...
title: Aldi to invest £900m in UK and open 40 more stores next year

author: Heather Stewart Economics editor
description:
With next month’s budget a month away, chancellor gives little indication in conference speech of where money will come from to reindustrialise Britain

  • Healey vows to stick to fiscal rules in budget

  • UK politics live – latest updates

John Healey cheered the Labour faithful with his first conference speech as chancellor, offering an upbeat vision of a reindustrialised Britain with fresh opportunities for young people – but gave little sense of how he intends to pay for Andy Burnham’s radical plans.

Healey’s budget next month is widely seen both inside and outside Labour as
title: Healey offers upbeat vision but sheds little light on how it will be paid for

author: Victoria Bekiempis
description:
Identity of man, 27, being withheld pending family notification after 700ft plunge

A Base jumper died on Sunday in Utah after his wingsuit failed while he plunged from a 700ft height, according to authorities.

Local news reports cited the Cache county sheriff’s office, which said that the man fell to his death at age 27 in a mountainous region of Hyrum, which is east from the city of Millville.

Continue reading...
title: Base jumper dies in Utah after wingsuit fails in remote mountainous region

author: Ben Beaumont-Thomas
description:
Previously unreleased material comes as Wonder marks 50th anniversary of album with arena tour

Stevie Wonder has expanded the scope of what was already the most epic studio album in his catalogue, 1976’s Songs in the Key of Life.

Four unheard songs from the recording sessions have been released today as a new EP of the same name, marking the 50th anniversary of an album which won album of the year at the Grammys and contains a number of Wonder’s landmark tracks including Sir Duke, As and Isn’t She Lovely.

Continue reading...
title: Stevie Wonder releases four unheard songs from Songs in the Key of Life sessions

author: Associated Press
description:
Powerful weather system pummels shoreline for a second day, knocking out power to tens of thousands

Residents of coastal communities in the US’s north-east slogged through floodwaters for a second day as a powerful storm known as a nor’easter pummeled the shoreline on Sunday, knocking out power to tens of thousands of homes.

Tidal surges swamped low-lying neighborhoods in New Jersey while wind gusts toppled trees on New York’s Long Island, damaging homes and bringing down utility poles.

Continue reading...
title: Nor’easter storm floods coastal areas from New Jersey to New England

author: Sara Sneath
description:
Fossil fuel firms have spent years trying to regulate climate research by donating to US universities, study authors argue

Recent attacks on US universities by the Trump administration have built on decades of efforts by libertarian donor networks, fossil fuel companies and conservative thinktanks to reshape university governance and increase outside influence, according to a new study.

The authors of the new perspective study argue that the erosion of university autonomy has left colleges more vulnerable to corporate interests, especially within climate and energy research.

Continue reading...
title: Decades of fossil fuel influence paved way for Trump’s assault on university research, study says

author: Robert Booth UK technology editor
description:
Exclusive: Instructors at tech training company Multiverse hit out at ‘remorseless’ and ‘unnerving’ monitoring system

Teachers at Euan Blair’s £1.6bn tech training company, Multiverse, have blown the whistle about “horrendous stress” and feeling constantly watched after bosses started using AI models to surveil and rate their teaching.

Staff delivering apprenticeship training in computer and AI skills to thousands of UK public and private sector workers now have transcripts of online classroom sessions analysed and scored by an AI programmed to alert human managers when they are suspected of doing things wrong.

Continue reading...
title: Teachers at Euan Blair firm report ‘horrendous stress’ after AI used to rate their work

author: Helena Horton
description:
Officers say they have secured extension to continue to hold men, all in their 20s, on suspicion of terror offences

Five men arrested on suspicion of terror offences at RAF Fairford are all British nationals from London in their 20s, counter-terrorism police have said.

The men were pictured on Sunday being apprehended, shirtless, near the RAF base in Gloucestershire, which is being used by the US air force in its operations against Iran.

Continue reading...
title: Five men arrested at RAF Fairford are all UK nationals from London, say police

author: Martin Belam
description:
Experts warn Republicans may try to sow distrust and claim ‘foreign interference’ in crucial hours after counting begins. Plus, two pandas have a new home thanks to US-China diplomacy

  • Don’t already get First Thing in your inbox? Sign up here

Good morning. Election experts have warned that Donald Trump’s administration could use the crucial hours and days after November’s midterm elections to disrupt the results after struggling to enforce the crackdown it wanted on voting.

After a succession of court setbacks to plans to restrict voting access, and with less than six weeks remaining until polls close, the post-election “counting window” is being seen as a particularly vulnerable moment by former US federal government officials.
title: ‘Counting window’ seen as high-risk time for Trump to cast doubt on midterm results | First Thing

author: Nick Visser
description:
The ocean phenomenon could raise sea levels by up to a foot as El Niño keeps warm water trapped along the coast

Concerns are mounting about an ocean phenomenon known as a kelvin wave that could raise sea levels along the California coastline by up to a foot, as scientists say El Niño is supercharging the threat of storm surges and flooding in the coming months.

As an incredibly strong El Niño continues to develop in the Pacific, the phenomenon brings with it a strange shift in the ocean. The kelvin wave phenomenon is created when trade winds that usually blow from South America towards Asia die down or reverse in El Niño years, setting off a massive, slow-moving slosh of water.

Continue reading...
title: Concern mounts over slow-moving, planetary-scale ‘kelvin’ wave heading for California

author: Steven Greenhouse
description:
Trump’s tariffs and his war against Iran caused prices to rise, but the US president continues to claim it’s ‘the greatest economy in history’

Donald Trump has taken to repeating a familiar boast: “We have the greatest economy in history,” Trump said recently at a White House press gaggle. The boast comes even though inflation is higher and economic growth lower than when Joe Biden left office, even though gas prices have jumped around 50% since the war against Iran started, and even though 73% of Americans think the economy is in fair or poor shape (48% say it’s in poor shape). What’s more, the Federal Reserve is so worried about inflation that it just raised interest rates.

“It’
title: As the US midterms approach, Trump’s boasts on the economy fall flat with voters

author: Samuel Firman
description:
River charters part of wider movement establishing ‘moral’ framework to protect nature and hold institutions to account

One Monday morning in spring last year, 12 people gathered in the morning drizzle at Joyce’s Pool, one of the sources of the Bristol River Avon, and took the first steps of the inaugural Avon pilgrimage.

Over the course of eight days, a revolving cast of pilgrims walked about 100 miles from the source of the river to the point at which it reaches the sea, in some cases bivvying on the riverside at night. Along the way they planted trees, sowed seeds, restored footpaths and presented councillors and decision-makers with a fledgling Avon charter, developed by the Bristol campaign group Conham Bathing.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Contract between humans and river’: Bristol Avon’s rights enshrined in charter

author: Rajeev Syal and agencies
description:
Dozens also reported injured after inflatable boat carrying 105 people gets into trouble off northern France

A child was among three people who died ⁠and dozens of others who were injured while ⁠attempting ​to cross the Channel on Monday, French authorities have said.

France’s maritime ​police ‌said ‌it received a ‌distress call in the early hours from an inflatable dinghy carrying 105 people that had ‌run into trouble in calm seas.

Continue reading...
title: Three people dead, including a child, in attempt to cross Channel to UK

author: Tom McIlroy Political editor
description:
Ballot for new leader expected next week after Waters quits to manage pre-existing kidney disease that has ‘declined significantly’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Greens leader Larissa Waters has announced she will step down due to ill health, with a party room meeting scheduled for next week to choose her successor.

Waters revealed on Monday night she has been managing a pre-existing kidney disease, but that her health had “declined significantly over the course of recent months”.

Get our new political email,
title: Larissa Waters steps down as Greens leader due to ill health

author: Ramon Antonio Vargas
description:
Social and news media commenters seize on senator’s gaffe, with some characterizing it as a Freudian slip

With speculation about whether he may defect from the Democratic party swirling around him, US senator John Fetterman described himself seemingly unintentionally as a “lifelong Republican” during a fireside chat in Texas over the weekend.

Fetterman made the comment when someone listening to him speak with CBS News political correspondent Major Garrett at the Texas Tribune Festival on Saturday asked the Pennsylvania senator why he had not become an independent.

Continue reading...
title: John Fetterman accidentally calls himself ‘a lifelong Republican’

author: Josh Taylor Technology reporter
description:
Developer Goodman Group says changes in government rules are behind decision to pull plug on ‘Project Mars’ in Lane Cove

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

Plans for a controversial $1.2bn datacentre in Lane Cove in Sydney’s north have been withdrawn, with the developer blaming “emerging” regulations from the state and federal governments for the decision to pull the plug.

The “Project Mars” plans were withdrawn from the NSW planning portal on Monday, with the developer, Goodman Group, posting on its site that the policy and regulatory environment for large-scale datacentres had “evolved significantly”.
title: Plan for controversial $1.2bn datacentre in Sydney scrapped due to ‘emerging’ regulations

author: Sarah Butler
description:
Jeweller reports flat sales and fall in underlying operating profit as retailers anticipate October budget

  • Business live – latest updates

The boss of family-owned jeweller Beaverbrooks has called on the government to give business “a bit of break” by halting cost increases amid flat sales and falling profits.

The retailer, founded in 1919, revealed a 9% fall in underlying operating profit to £7.8m last year after an increase in employer national insurance contributions (NICs) and the legal minimum wage introduced by former chancellor Rachel Reeves.

Continue reading...
title: Boss of Beaverbrooks urges government to give businesses ‘a bit of a break’

author: Australian Associated Press
description:
Local authorities have closed the beach for several kilometres and multiple sharks have been spotted in the area

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Multiple sharks have been spotted swimming near a large, smelly whale carcass that has washed ashore at a popular capital city beach, drawing hundreds of onlookers.

Surf lifesavers found the dead animal at Perth’s City beach at about 7.30am on Monday and raised the alarm.

Continue reading...
title: After a dead whale washed up at a Perth beach, some took selfies. Others held their nose from the stench

author: Josh Taylor and Tom McIlroy
description:
Company behind Claude chatbot expected to attend separate Australian government hearing on AI next week

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

The chief executive of Anthropic will turn down an invitation to appear at a Senate committee hearing on AI this week, in the wake of the revelation that OpenAI agents had breached Australian government websites.

However, the company will make an appearance before another committee early next week.

Sign up for Guardian Australia’s Politics, really newsletter here
title: Anthropic will not appear at Senate inquiry into AI and datacentres amid fallout from OpenAI hack

author: Andrew Sparrow
description:
Healey to announce new facilities to maintain nuclear submarines on the Clyde

Andy Burnham’s plans to reform social care could cost far more than he is claiming and take “many decades” to be implemented, a leading expert has claimed.

Andrew Dilnot told the Today programme this morning that he was “puzzled” by some of what Burnham said yesterday, and he implied that he was unconvinced by what Burnham was offering.

[Burnham] did talk about making social care free, and what he implied was that he wanted social care to be completely free.

And that’s not at all the case in Scotland, where although the policy is called free personal care, we still have exactly the problem that Mr Burnham himself has talked about of people needing residential care faced with very substantial bills.

It sounds as though there’ll be some more details [of the plans] in the prime minister’s speech tomorrow at his party conference, but I think even that will conti
title: Chancellor John Healey to promise ‘new age of industrialisation’ in speech to Labour conference – UK politics live

author: Yohannes Lowe
description:
Five men arrested over terrorism offences after explosives found near base

Good morning and welcome to our coverage of events at RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire as counter-terrorism police investigate whether Iran is behind a suspected bomb plot at the base which is used by the US military to carry out missions in the Middle East.

Five men detained near the base early on Sunday were initially detained over explosives offences and then were further arrested later in the day on suspicion of the preparation of a terrorist act. Pictures of the men with their shirts off could point to a precautionary measure against the risk of suicide vests or concealed weapons.

Continue reading...
title: RAF Fairford live updates: police investigate Iran link to suspected bomb plot

author: Lauren Almeida
description:
Rail operator linking London to Birmingham, the north-west and Glasgow had highest number of cancellations across network

Avanti West Coast will be renationalised in spring, as Andy Burnham declares “enough is enough” for passengers who have put up with a rail service “that has failed them time and time again”.

The rail operator, which is one of the worst in the country for train delays and cancellations, will come under public ownership from March when its contract ends.

Swarms of bogong moths have surprised New South Wales residents over the last few days – with experts saying sightings of the endangered native insect are cause for excitement rather than alarm.

Hundreds of moth sightings in coastal areas were posted over the weekend to the iNaturalist page for Bogong Watch, a citizen science initiative run by Invertebrates Australia.
